checks.question: For one piece of TDF content, who creates it, who checks facts and permissions, who can publish it, and who keeps track of the result?

checks.question: For a specific event, service or funding agreement, which entity would make the commitment, who can sign it, and what approval must happen first?

checks.question: What can Jaggy help connect or improve during this stewardship, and if a small AI service proves useful, who would willingly operate and support it afterwards?

maps.title: AI and technology revenue
maps.subtitle: Useful work and reliable cowork now; events, AI and hosting offers to test.
maps.intro: Human flourishing is the purpose. Reliable workspaces, usable knowledge and clear access support five possible wins. Named offers and references below are dated evidence or proposals; none establishes a new customer, committed service or income.

groups.title: Shared TDF foundation
groups.description: Working connectivity, power, records and access support daily work.

groups.title: Offers to improve or test
groups.description: Cowork first; gatherings and future hosting serve specific users.

groups.title: Who operates and owns it?
groups.description: TDF, an independent business and a partner are alternative models.

groups.title: Five wins to work toward
groups.description: Useful work, new people, income, a 2027 event and an enduring identity.

groups.title: Concrete knowledge reuse
groups.description: Inspect existing tools and approaches before creating another system.

nodes.label: Fixed line + Wi-Fi
nodes.summary: Test existing connectivity for reliable work; fixed-line timing remains uncertain.
details: The October 9 meeting reported a possible year-long fixed-line delay. This is an estimate from the meeting, not a provider-confirmed schedule.
Near-term cowork and small learning experiments can use existing permitted connectivity after a real test. A hosting service needs evidence of capacity and reliability.
questions: What can the current connection support during real calls and concurrent work?

nodes.label: Power and reliability
nodes.summary: Existing solar and storage are a foundation; suitability for further compute needs testing.
details: The equipment is reported in existing sources. Availability for additional workloads, resilience and operating cost remain separate checks.
questions: What power can the proposed workload use without disrupting existing needs?

nodes.label: Shared records / access
nodes.summary: Findable shared records can make current TDF work easier.
details: Reuse existing source homes and access routes. Documentation is useful when a real person can find, understand and use it for an actual task.
questions: Which practical task needs a source-linked result first?

nodes.label: Roles and permissions
nodes.summary: Ownership, permission, support and repair routes need to be clear.
details: A person with useful knowledge is not automatically the authorised operator or budget owner.
questions: Who can authorise, maintain and recover each service?

related.label: Named people and open role boundaries

nodes.label: Local compute capacity
nodes.summary: Local AI or server capacity is a future option.
details: A deployed paid compute cluster is not established. Existing systems do not by themselves establish the capacity, data permissions or support needed for a new offer.
questions: What useful task actually needs local compute?

nodes.label: Hosting and storage
nodes.summary: Hosting storage and a NAS remain options, with no new deployment established.
details: Compare existing permitted storage and maintained hosted options against the actual use before choosing hardware.
questions: What must be stored, with which permissions, backup and recovery?

nodes.label: Reliable coworking
nodes.summary: Reliable cowork is the near-term experience to improve.
details: One private guest interview points to working-condition friction alongside the appeal of nature and community. This is qualitative input, not validated pricing or a demand forecast.
questions: Can real cowork users complete calls and focused work comfortably?

nodes.label: Work-friendly stays
nodes.summary: Work-friendly stays could build on reliable cowork and the TDF setting.
details: A proposed improvement to the visitor experience. Suite bundles, premium access and new prices are later hypotheses; no approved construction or commercial package is established.
questions: Which visitor would return or pay for a clearly described improvement?

nodes.label: AI / nature learning
nodes.summary: Explore a small November technology and human-flourishing gathering.
details: A meetup, practical test day, focused hackathon or facilitated weekend are alternatives. Audience, format, willing hosts, date and cost are open.
The October 9 meeting broadens this beyond the earlier Meshtastic idea. A first gathering may establish participation without paid attendance.
questions: Which single audience and useful experience should the first experiment serve?

nodes.label: Meshtastic visitors
nodes.summary: An earlier radio-related visitor/event lead through Nuno remains unconfirmed.
details: Keep attendance, people, dates and equipment unresolved. A radio exercise would need that dependency; a broader November gathering does not automatically depend on it.
questions: Is a specific radio activity wanted and are suitable people and equipment available?

nodes.label: Local hosting / AI use
nodes.summary: Future local hosting or AI access could become a paid offer.
details: Requires tested capacity, permissions, upkeep, recovery and actual users. No live paid service, customer or revenue is established.
questions: Who would use and pay for one specific reliable service?

nodes.label: Optional paid support
nodes.summary: Optional paid technology operation or support is a discussion idea.
details: For example, operating accounts or hosted tools for others. This has not been selected as Jaggy’s business or assigned as a stewardship duty.
questions: Does a concrete user need ongoing support and who would carry that obligation?

nodes.label: TDF-operated offer
nodes.summary: TDF could operate an offer and carry its obligations.
details: One alternative business model. Entity, payment recipient, costs, support and authority require agreement before describing it as an active offer.
questions: Which TDF entity could authorise and operate the chosen offer?

nodes.label: Jaggy's business
nodes.summary: An independent Jaggy business could use agreed TDF facilities.
details: A proposed alternative to TDF operating an offer. Space rental and infrastructure use would require specific terms; no contract is established.
questions: What would TDF provide and what would the independent operator own?

nodes.label: Partner-led offer
nodes.summary: A partner could operate an offer under agreed terms.
details: Another alternative operator model, not an identified committed partner.
questions: Is there a capable willing operator for a defined offer?

nodes.label: Written arrangement
nodes.summary: A written arrangement should define use, costs, support and exit.
details: TDF foundations and business responsibilities are different obligations. Operator alternatives must not be added together as forecast income.
questions: Who owns the hardware, receives payment and handles failure or departure?

nodes.label: Hardware ownership
nodes.summary: Hardware ownership and use rights remain open.
details: Equipment finance does not settle purchasing authority, ownership or community access.
questions: Who would buy and own the equipment?

details: A future service creates continuing work and costs after installation.
questions: Who can maintain the service throughout its operating life?

questions: What capacity would the actual use require?

questions: Can the exact equipment-finance source and proposed terms be recovered?

questions: Is a capable team and eligible science/safety project present?

nodes.summary: Actual users, payers and repeat interest need evidence.
details: A website, guest interview or possible visitor is not proof of a market. Start with one real use and record what happens.
questions: Who will try the smallest permitted version and return?

nodes.summary: Compare full operating cost before an offer or hardware decision.
details: Include support time, energy, hardware life, space, connectivity and recovery; grants or loan principal are not recurring revenue.
questions: Can a small offer cover the work and obligations it creates?

groups.description: Recover proposals, entity, owner and one credible project.

groups.title: Comparators and pending references
groups.description: Secondary examples; no additional TDF funding claim.

nodes.label: TDF fundraiser
nodes.summary: TDF publishes several ways to back the place.
details: The fundraiser page was checked October 9. A published mechanism does not prove money received, unrestricted cash or current legal terms.
questions: What receipts, restrictions and obligations exist for each route?

nodes.label: Token backing
nodes.summary: Token backing is a published access/governance route.
details: Use and governance rights need current terms. Dividends or profit shares must not be inferred from token language.
questions: What current rights and intended use does the actual backing provide?

nodes.label: Private lending
nodes.summary: Private lending is a published financing route.
details: Borrowing carries repayment and approval obligations. No lender, liability amount or new loan is established here.
questions: Who is the borrower and what approved terms and obligations apply?

nodes.label: Prepaid stays
nodes.summary: Prepaid stays offer advance cash with future accommodation owed.
details: An advance purchase is distinct from a donation, a grant and unrestricted earned income.
questions: What future stays or services must be delivered?

nodes.label: Monthly support
nodes.summary: Monthly backing is a published recurring-support route.
details: Subscribers, product terms, restrictions and actual receipts are unverified.
questions: What support is active and what obligations accompany it?

nodes.label: Current funding ledger
nodes.summary: The current received, restricted and owed position needs recovery.
details: Use existing finance records and proposal owners. Public campaign pages cannot substitute for receipts or a cash ledger.
questions: Which existing owner can establish current funding and commitments?

nodes.label: OASA Village Fund
nodes.summary: OASA advertises a Village Fund and Artizen matching model.
details: The October 9 Artizen destination returned no readable live pool data. TDF participation, usable allocation and conditions are unestablished.
questions: Is TDF participating and what current pool and conditions apply?

nodes.label: OASA catalytic capital
nodes.summary: OASA describes donations, patient loans and repayable grants.
details: This is a separate model from the Village Fund donation layer. Operator projections are not checked transfers or a TDF award.
questions: Which instrument, if any, is currently active for TDF?

nodes.label: Ma Earth
nodes.summary: Ma Earth nature-project matching is a future dated lead.
details: October 9 research recorded an opening on22April2027. This date is not refreshed today; a community-supported project and applicant still need fit review.
questions: Does a bounded land project match the actual current route?

nodes.label: ReFi / Localism Fund
nodes.summary: ReFi / Localism Fund has a documented local grant-programme model.
details: The retained launch account is historical. A current round and deadline were not verified; it is not established as a grant to purchase TDF sensors.
questions: Which current programme, if any, is relevant to a local funding hub?

nodes.label: One Project
nodes.summary: One Project announced a Common Action Fund for 2027.
details: The October 9 partner route is a future/partnership lead rather than an established open TDF grant.
questions: What actual partnership or call conditions apply?

nodes.label: Monty + August
nodes.summary: Monty and August are knowledge routes for water and ReFi context.
details: Reported expertise and work grouping do not assign finance authority, grant approval or an application duty.
questions: What existing ecological or funding work should be recovered first?

related.label: Knowledge routes and separate role authority

nodes.label: ADL / PEPAC
nodes.summary: ADL / PEPAC is a dated local-investment lead with incomplete eligibility review.
details: October 9 official listing recorded a23October2026,17:00 close. It has not been refreshed today.
The full notice was not obtained. Territory, activity, eligible costs and co-funding still require review.
questions: Does the full current notice fit a real project and capable applicant?

nodes.label: Mozilla Incubator
nodes.summary: Mozilla Incubator supports working community technology; retain as a dated future lead.
details: October 9 research recorded a forthcoming2027 cohort. No current open call, eligible TDF product or application is established.
questions: Is there a working tool with early community value and a matching actual call?

nodes.label: Foresight Local Compute
nodes.summary: Foresight Local Compute is a dated science/safety research lead.
details: October 9 research recorded31October2026,23:59PDT as the close. This listing is not refreshed today.
Requires credible execution, science/safety alignment and open outputs. It is not general Mac Studio or November-event funding.
questions: Is a bounded eligible project and capable team present?

related.label: Future capacity; no grant or deployment established

nodes.label: Erasmus+ learning
nodes.summary: Erasmus+ can support an eligible learning partnership.
details: The youth-worker mobility route needs eligible organisations and a genuine youth-work purpose. It is not a commercial retreat or general venue subsidy; no new current TDF call is established.
questions: Are actual partners, purpose and agency round eligible?

nodes.label: Charlie's NEB plan
nodes.summary: Charlie’s September Connect NEB plan is historical proposal context.
details: The earlier programme and proposal context can inform future community-participation or living-lab work. It establishes no current call or new award.
questions: Which lessons from the earlier community-participation proposal are useful?

nodes.label: Start PME
nodes.summary: Start PME is publicly listed for Grant Support.
details: The October 9 team page supports the listing, not an active mandate, prior contact or submission receipt.
questions: What current engagement and application records exist?

nodes.label: Anura Capital
nodes.summary: Anura describes regenerative real-estate investment and advisory.
details: This is a commercial/partnership model rather than a generic grant. TDF mandate and Portugal allocation are not established.
questions: Would any actual mandate match the project’s ownership and return needs?

nodes.label: Rebalance Earth
nodes.summary: Rebalance Earth structures natural-capital and outcome investment.
details: Requires credible measurement, long-term delivery and a paying counterparty. TDF/Portugal suitability is unestablished.
questions: Is there an actual paid ecological outcome and suitable mandate?

nodes.label: Paying beneficiary
nodes.summary: A paying beneficiary for an ecological outcome has not been identified.
details: Environmental value alone does not establish a buyer, contract or payment.
questions: Who would pay for which measured outcome?

nodes.label: Capital obligations
nodes.summary: Each capital instrument carries different obligations.
details: Donations, loans, pre-sales, token backing and outcome contracts differ in repayment, use rights and control. Do not add them as available cash.
questions: What duties and approvals accompany the selected instrument?

nodes.label: Portugal / project fit
nodes.summary: Territory, entity and project fit remain route-specific.
details: TDF, OASA and Enseada are distinct. A shared interest in regeneration does not establish a funding mandate.
questions: Which applicant and place qualify for the actual route?

nodes.label: Costs beyond a grant
nodes.summary: Account for costs beyond the grant.
details: Cash timing, co-funding, work capacity and long-term upkeep can remain after an award.
questions: Can the project be delivered and maintained on its actual cash schedule?

nodes.label: Existing land work
nodes.summary: Existing water, wells, soil and stewardship work is the starting point.
details: Dated source accounts need expert correction and practical use. A documented routine can help before any grant or new sensor system.
questions: What useful land task has a willing practitioner and reviewer?

related.label: Evidence systems do not establish physical field health

nodes.label: Ecology Repositree
nodes.summary: Ecology Repositree retains source-linked places, projects and data.
details: The inspected local snapshot is a dated source home. It is distinct from Closer and is not a claim of complete live integration.
questions: Which current source and maintainer support the chosen project?

nodes.label: Baseline + outcome
nodes.summary: A credible outcome needs a baseline, method and uncertainty.
details: Modelled projections, recorded observations and measured outcomes must remain distinct.
questions: What before/after evidence can a capable owner actually maintain?

nodes.label: Digital + people maps
nodes.summary: Findable records and clear access support ecological continuity.
details: The digital and people maps can expose missing access and stewardship routes without inventing permissions.
questions: Can the real practitioner find and use the permitted evidence?

nodes.label: Permitted evidence
nodes.summary: Evidence needs permission, attribution and a correction route.
details: Documentation is not consent to upload raw records, publish personal media or sell carbon/biodiversity credits.
questions: Which evidence can be used, by whom and for which purpose?

nodes.label: Delivery capacity
nodes.summary: A named willing maintainer and credible scope need confirmation.
details: A grant or tool does not create practitioner capacity. Existing residents are not automatically delivery staff.
questions: Who will do, review and maintain the work?

nodes.label: Applicant / signatory
nodes.summary: Applicant and signatory must be identified for the selected route.
details: TDF, Enseada and OASA are not interchangeable payment or legal recipients. Public descriptions do not settle legal status or authority.
questions: Which actual entity/person is eligible and authorised to sign?

nodes.label: Existing proposals
nodes.summary: Recover existing proposals, decisions and receipts before adding work.
details: Historical governance captures can disagree with current descriptions. Existing ownership and actual submission evidence take priority.
questions: What is already proposed, submitted, decided or obligated?

nodes.label: One fundable project
nodes.summary: Choose one bounded ecological project before matching funding.
details: State the place, practical outcome, owner, cost, evidence and permitted outputs. No two-month application commitment is inferred.
questions: Which project can a real team credibly deliver?

nodes.label: Pursue / later / not fit
nodes.summary: Classify routes as pursue, later or not fit with reasons.
details: A logo inventory is not eligibility or an application queue. Prioritise source recovery and one concrete fit test.
questions: What evidence changes a lead into a decision?

nodes.label: Decision record
nodes.summary: Record the source date, status, owner route and next result.
details: Preparation, submission, acceptance, payment and completed delivery are distinct states.
questions: What is the next evidence-backed state for the chosen lead?

nodes.label: AI / tech revenue map
nodes.summary: Earned AI/tech income remains a separate route.
details: Loan/grant capital is not customer revenue; new visitors without payment do not establish income.
questions: Which actual customer payment belongs in the income record?

nodes.label: NLnet · Restack lead
nodes.summary: A dated lead for a reusable open-source improvement.
details: October 9 review recorded3November2026,12:00CET/11:00Lisbon. The specific call and policy must be rechecked before application.
R&D, eligible open outputs, a capable maintainer/team and programme-specific European fit are required. Installing an existing tool alone does not establish fit.
Restack’s recorded AI restrictions, AI-assistance disclosure and milestone payment limits matter. Generic event sponsorship and immediate November cash are not established.
questions: What reusable missing capability, existing project and eligible team fit the actual current call?

nodes.label: TDF biochar / pyrolysis plan
nodes.summary: An existing published ecological project needs current status recovery.
details: October 9 research found a late 2026 target with heat and biochar specifications. These are published targets, not installed equipment or measured production. Keep biochar sales, avoided heat cost and certified removal income separate.
questions: Who owns the current proposal and what equipment, feedstock, labour, buyer and verification evidence exists?

nodes.label: FarmTree
nodes.summary: A possible agroforestry modelling/research connection offered by Matthijs.
details: Matthijs’s October 10 collaboration account and introduction offer remain reported. No introduction, TDF partnership, selected tool or joint application is established. Modelled scenarios are not measured TDF outcomes or credit eligibility.
FarmTree is distinct from the supplied xFarm reference and the already-known farmOS. Those tools have not been compared or selected here.
questions: Is there a concrete land question, suitable input data and useful research fit?

nodes.label: Balloon Latam
nodes.summary: A Chile-focused learning reference outside the active Portugal shortlist.
details: Dated source screening did not establish a Portugal funding route. Retain as background rather than an additional grant to pursue.
questions: Is there a transferable participation lesson rather than funding fit?

nodes.label: Klein Jasedow
nodes.summary: A rural-centre mixed-support comparator attributed to Charlie.
details: The forwarded account names Sona Gong Manufaktur, Oya Medien eG, Drachen Verlag, Allmendhof, Lassaner Winkel Village School and European Academy of Healing Arts projects. Their legal, donor and cash relationships are unverified; no TDF funding offer is established.
questions: What support and work actually sustain the centre?

nodes.label: DisCO
nodes.summary: A supplied governance/work-compensation reference awaiting review.
details: Its manifesto link is retained; no operating model is adopted and no funding fit is established.
questions: Which concrete practice could help a bounded contribution decision?

edges.label: Potential reusable open-source improvement; fit to test
Recover existing project before a new funding case
Possible modelling support; method and inputs to assess

checks.result: The eligible authorised recipient for one chosen commitment.

checks.question: Recover biochar’s current project evidence.
checks.result: Actual proposal, equipment status, operating capacity and cost boundaries.

checks.question: Review a dated call only against a real project.
checks.who: Existing funding owner / capable delivery team
checks.result: Current official notice and a reasoned fit or no-fit decision.

checks.question: Screen the FarmTree offer against a practical land question.
checks.result: Input/method/terms fit; any introduction remains a separate next action.

checks.question: Choose and document a maintainable ecological result.
checks.result: Useful task, baseline, permitted evidence and continuing maintainer.

checks.result: A decision record separating awards, loans, future services and actual revenue.
